READING THE RULES

Different instruments have different legal effects

10 / 29

Binding requirements

Acts, regulations and binding regulatory requirements create duties for the relevant activity.

Supervisory expectations

Guidance may explain existing law or inform supervisory assessment and corrective action.

Voluntary frameworks

Methods and guidance for organising controls. Contracts or policies may add commitments.

Start with the legal form of the instrument. Acts, regulations and binding regulatory requirements create enforceable duties within their scope. They can apply to AI-enabled activities even when written before the technology became common.

Supervisory statements and guidance require closer reading. Some explain how a regulator interprets existing law; others set expectations for firms under its supervision.

An instrument may be non-binding in itself while influencing assessment or corrective action under the regulator's powers. The instrument and legal authority determine consequences, including whether a penalty applies.

Voluntary frameworks provide methods and recommended practices. Contracts or policies may create additional commitments. These categories can overlap for a single use. They are not three risk levels, and every use need not fall under all three.
